root_cause.text: The mutex field in struct apple_smc was never initialized via mutex_init(), causing uninitialized mutex state that could lead to NULL pointer dereferences when sub-device probe functions called apple_smc_read() and attempted to acquire the lock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a single line `mutex_init(&smc->mutex);` immediately after allocating the apple_smc structure in apple_smc_probe(). The CVE description explicitly states that "using the mutex uninitialized surprisingly resulted only in occasional NULL pointer dereferences in apple_smc_read() calls from the probe() functions of sub devices," indicating that the mutex was being used without proper initialization. The original code at commit e038d985c9823 allocated the structure but failed to call mutex_init() on the embedded mutex field before it was accessed by concurrent sub-device probes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the smc->mutex lock immediately after structure allocation to prevent undefined behavior from uninitialized mutex operations.
intent_record.what: Added a `mutex_init(&smc->mutex)` call immediately after memory allocation and before other field initialization in the apple_smc_probe function.
intent_record.how: This initializes the mutex lock associated with the smc structure early in the probe sequence, ensuring the mutex is properly set up before any code path that might attempt to acquire it. Without this initialization, subsequent mutex operations (lock/unlock) would operate on uninitialized memory, causing undefined behavior or crashes.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability root cause is that the mutex field in struct apple_smc is never initialized via mutex_init(). Examining the apple_smc_probe() function (lines 420-498), we can see that while completions are initialized with init_completion(&smc->init_done) and init_completion(&smc->cmd_done) at lines 451-452, there is NO corresponding mutex_init(&smc->mutex) call. The mutex is used throughout the code via guard(mutex)(&smc->mutex) in functions like apple_smc_cmd() (line 109), apple_smc_read() (line 165), apple_smc_write() (line 173), apple_smc_rw() (line 181), and apple_smc_enter_atomic() (line 201). The struct apple_smc is allocated with devm_kzalloc() (line 428), which zero-initializes it, but this does not properly initialize the mutex. Without mutex_init(), the mutex remains in an uninitialized state, which can lead to NULL pointer dereferences or undefined behavior when sub-device probe functions call apple_smc_read() and attempt to acquire the lock via guard(mutex)(&smc->mutex).
